root.name: Ponziani Opening: Ponziani Countergambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. c3 f5

overview: Black meets 3.c3 with 3...f5, a countergambit at once attacking the e4 pawn. The main line 4.d4 d6 5.d5 fxe4 6.Ng5 Nb8 7.Nxe4 Nf6 8.Bd3 gives White the better centre and development, with Black's king-side loosened. It is sharp, but strong players regard it as dubious for Black.

white_ideas.idea: Play d4 and d5 to gain space and kick the knight
Take on e4 with the knight and develop Bd3 and O-O
Use the weak e6 and g6 squares and the open f-file

black_ideas.idea: Take on e4 and rely on ...Nf6 and ...Be7
Counter on the f-file or by ...e4 to release the tension

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with a White space edge and a Black loosened kingside
White d5 pawn cramping the Black pieces

character.notes: Early counterattack with open lines and mutual tactics.

gambit.notes: The 3...f5 countergambit lets White take on f5 or e5, and Black plays for tempo and the f-file.

soundness.notes: White gets a clear advantage with d4-d5 and the extra tempo.

structure.notes: Pawns come off in the centre and the pieces play on open lines.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom play 3...f5; it is a surprise try.

level.notes: Black needs to know the main line; dubious, so not for beginners.
